lesson_title: Solving Problems Involving Surface Area, Volume and Capacity
hook_text: Thirty boxes should fit by volume. Packed one way, only eighteen do.
clip_script:
How many small boxes fit into a large carton? Dividing the volumes gives an upper limit, but boxes are rigid, so the true number depends on how they line up. The carton is 60 by 40 by 30 centimetres; the boxes are 20 by 15 by 8. The volumes say 30.

Pack them one way: 3 along, 2 across with a gap, 3 up with a gap — only 18. Turn them: 3 along, 5 across, 2 up — exactly 30. Divide each dimension, round down, multiply, and try the turns. Volume tells you the limit; the dimensions tell you the truth.
visual_style: A cardboard carton fills with boxes in one orientation leaving visible gaps, empties, then fills perfectly with the boxes turned
